title: Phoenix leads the nation in fatal police shootings
summary: Phoenix officers were involved in 44 shootings in 2018, 23 of them fatal. That was the most fatal officer-involved shootings of any U.S. municipal agency that year, compared with an average of about 23 shootings a year from 2009 to 2017.

title: Republic investigation: Phoenix outpaces peer cities in shootings
summary: An Arizona Republic analysis found Phoenix police shootings had surpassed those in comparable cities for years. Houston, a larger city, had 18 shootings in 2018 to Phoenix's 44.

title: Council votes 5-4 for civilian oversight (OAT)
summary: Phoenix City Council approved the Office of Accountability and Transparency and a community review board, after a five-hour meeting.

title: Protesters charged as a 'criminal street gang'
summary: Phoenix police arrested 18 protesters, including three minors, and county prosecutors charged them with assisting a criminal street gang. ABC15's 'Politically Charged' investigation exposed the grand jury testimony behind the charges.

title: Prosecutors drop the protest gang case
summary: Maricopa County Attorney Allister Adel moved to dismiss case CR 2020-139581, about a week after ABC15 published the grand jury transcript.

title: OAT ordinance adopted
summary: The City Council adopted Ordinance G-6851, creating Chapter 20 of the city code and giving OAT its powers. A November 2020 version had failed 5-4.

title: Judge finds police and prosecutors 'colluded' before the grand jury
summary: Judge Jennifer Ryan-Touhill dismissed the gang charges with prejudice, finding that Sgt. Doug McBride and prosecutor April Sponsel 'colluded in their efforts to present the grand jury with false information regarding a non-existent gang.'

title: DOJ opens a pattern-or-practice investigation
summary: The U.S. Justice Department's Civil Rights Division opened an investigation into the City of Phoenix and the Phoenix Police Department.

title: DOJ findings: excessive force and discrimination
summary: DOJ found reasonable cause to believe Phoenix police use excessive force, including unjustified deadly force; unlawfully detain and arrest people experiencing homelessness; discriminate against Black, Hispanic and Native American people; violate protest rights; and discriminate against people with behavioral health disabilities.

title: DOJ closes the investigation and retracts its findings
summary: Under the Trump administration, the Civil Rights Division closed the Phoenix investigation and retracted the 2024 findings, without a consent decree. City leaders said reforms would continue anyway.
